original_question: Let mu be a nonnegative continuous majorant on [-1,1], and let omega_mu in P_n be the associated snake polynomial, meaning the unique degree-n polynomial that oscillates most between plus and minus mu at an alternation set. Find a class of majorants mu for which the associated snake polynomials Q_n have a Chebyshev expansion Q_n = sum_{i=0}^n a_i T_i whose coefficients are either all nonnegative or strictly sign-alternating, in the sense that a_i a_{i+1} < 0 for every i.
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the Open problem in Geno Nikolov’s section "Snake polynomials with positive Chebyshev expansions," with the immediately following Conjecture (G.N.) providing the paper’s specific proposed class of majorants.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main objects from the targeted section: a majorant on [-1,1], the associated snake polynomial, expansion in Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind, and the two sign-pattern regimes the paper asks about (non-negative coefficients or alternating signs). It also correctly captures that the problem is to single out a class of majorants for which this coefficient behavior occurs.
missing_details: The paper’s nearest official formulation is first an open problem ('Find a class of majorants...') and then, separately, a conjectured answer in one direction: if μ is continuous, even, and convex on [-1,1], then the associated snake polynomials should have non-negative Chebyshev expansion.
The paper defines P_n as the set of real algebraic polynomials of degree at most n; this ambient class should be stated explicitly.
The snake polynomial is unique only up to orientation (overall sign), so any coefficient-sign condition should be stated up to an overall sign choice.

To make the question stand-alone, one should spell out the defining alternation property: for the n-th snake polynomial ω_{n,μ}, one has |ω_{n,μ}(x)| ≤ μ(x) on [-1,1], and there exist n+1 alternation points τ_0 < ··· < τ_n in [-1,1] such that ω_{n,μ}(τ_i) = (-1)^i μ(τ_i), after fixing an orientation.

The quantifier over n is implicit in the paper: it speaks about the associated snake polynomials (plural), i.e. the n-th snake polynomial for each relevant degree n. Your draft does not say whether the property is meant for one fixed n or uniformly for all n.
Your notation switches from ω_μ to Q_n; the paper does not introduce that switch, so the notation should be made consistent.

The phrase 'sign alternating' in the paper should not be sharpened to the strict condition a_i a_{i+1} < 0 unless separately justified; the paper only says 'sign alternating' and does not, in this section, impose strict nonvanishing of consecutive coefficients.

The general open problem in the paper is about majorants without explicitly imposing continuity; continuity enters the adjacent conjecture through the narrower class of continuous even convex majorants. Your draft merges these two scopes.
refined_question: For each n ≥ 1, let P_n be the space of real algebraic polynomials of degree at most n, and let μ:[-1,1]→[0,∞) be a majorant for which the n-th snake polynomial ω_{n,μ} exists, meaning that ω_{n,μ}∈P_n is unique up to overall sign, satisfies |ω_{n,μ}(x)|≤μ(x) for all x∈[-1,1], and has an alternation set τ_0<⋯<τ_n in [-1,1] with ω_{n,μ}(τ_i)=(-1)^i μ(τ_i) after choosing an orientation. Characterize the majorants μ for which, for every such n, one can choose the orientation of ω_{n,μ} so that its expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind, ω_{n,μ}(x)=∑_{i=0}^n a_i T_i(x), is either coefficientwise non-negative (a_i≥0 for all i) or sign-alternating in the Chebyshev basis (equivalently, up to overall sign, (-1)^i a_i≥0 for all i). In particular, is this property guaranteed when μ is continuous, even, and convex on [-1,1], and in that case does one always get the non-negative alternative?
justification: The draft is closest to the section’s stated Open problem, because it asks to 'find a class of majorants' for which the associated snake polynomials have either non-negative or sign-alternating Chebyshev expansion. The paper then immediately records a sharper conjectural candidate class—continuous even convex μ on [-1,1]—for which only the non-negative alternative is predicted. The surrounding lines in the same section supply the needed notation: P_n is the class of real algebraic polynomials of degree at most n; the snake polynomial is defined via a uniform majorization condition together with an alternation set; and the motivation is that such coefficient-sign patterns are known to force extremality in the Markov and Duffin–Schaeffer majorant problems. Your draft is mathematically close, but to be fully paper-faithful it needs the paper’s distinction between the general open problem and the specific conjectured class, the quantifier over n, the orientation issue, and a weaker formulation of 'sign alternating' than strict adjacent sign changes.
